note: checked=true means the source page was opened and read on the date above (URL, license and structure as listed). checked=false means the entry comes from the dataset's paper or common knowledge of the field and was not re-opened that day; open the URL before relying on details. Column hints are hints: print the header first.

datasets.name: LLMail-Inject (Microsoft): adaptive prompt-injection attacks on an email assistant
datasets.format: JSON / Parquet; splits Phase1 (~371k rows) and Phase2 (~91k rows)
datasets.notes: Each row is an attacker-written email. `objectives` is a JSON string of flags such as email.retrieved, defense.undetected, exfil.sent that say how far the attack got. Paper: arXiv 2506.09956. Analysis code: github.com/microsoft/llmail-inject-challenge-analysis.

datasets.name: InjecAgent: 1,054 indirect prompt-injection test cases for tool-using agents
datasets.format: JSON test cases in the repo's data/ folder (17 user tools, 62 attacker tools)
datasets.notes: Single-turn cases: a user task, a tool response containing an injected instruction, and the attacker's goal (direct harm or data stealing). Easy to replay against your own guard. Paper: arXiv 2403.02691.

datasets.name: AgentDojo: dynamic environment for agent prompt-injection attacks and defenses
datasets.format: Python package with four suites: workspace (email/calendar), travel, banking, slack
datasets.notes: Heavier than the others: budget 15 minutes for setup. Use it if you want a full agent loop with tools. Docs: https://agentdojo.spylab.ai. Paper: arXiv 2406.13352.

datasets.name: deepset/prompt-injections: small labeled set of injection vs. benign prompts
datasets.format: A few hundred rows with text and a 0/1 label
datasets.notes: Good as a quick benign/attack sanity set and as a source of benign text for false-positive checks.

datasets.name: AgentHarm (UK AI Security Institute): harmful multi-step agent tasks with benign counterparts
datasets.license: See dataset card (may require accepting terms)
datasets.format: JSON behaviors with tool definitions
datasets.notes: Use to check that an agent refuses harmful tool-use tasks while still completing the matched benign ones.

fetch.instructions: Open the dataset card, accept terms if asked, then: from datasets import load_dataset; load_dataset('ai-safety-institute/AgentHarm', 'harmful')

datasets.name: NHTSA Standing General Order crash reports: Automated Driving Systems (current file, June 16 2025 onward)
datasets.format: CSV, one row per report version; monthly updates
datasets.notes: Filter State == CA and City == San Francisco. The same crash can appear several times (report versions, multiple reporting entities): de-duplicate before counting. Some narratives are redacted as confidential business information. Reports are unverified and there is no mileage denominator. Read the data dictionary PDF first.

datasets.name: NHTSA SGO crash reports: ADS archive (2021 to June 15 2025)
datasets.format: CSV
datasets.notes: Older schema than the current file; column names differ. Combine with care.

datasets.name: NHTSA SGO crash reports: Level 2 driver assistance (ADAS)
datasets.format: CSV
datasets.notes: Driver-assist systems in consumer cars, not robotaxis. Reporting criteria differ from ADS, so do not compare counts directly.

datasets.name: Augmented dataset of autonomous vehicle collisions in California, 2019–2024
datasets.format: One CSV, about 670 kB
datasets.notes: Researchers turned the CA DMV collision report PDFs into a table and added GIS and LLM-extracted fields. The fastest way to get structured California AV collision data. Ends Dec 31 2024.

datasets.name: California DMV autonomous vehicle collision reports (form OL 316)
datasets.format: One PDF per collision, listed by company and date (2019 onward)
datasets.notes: Covers vehicles under testing permits. Use for 2025–2026 reports that the Zenodo table does not cover: download 5–10 PDFs and extract with Claude.

fetch.instructions: Open the page, pick recent PDFs, save to data/ca-dmv-collision-reports/.

datasets.name: California DMV autonomous vehicle disengagement and mileage reports
datasets.format: CSV per year (disengagements and mileage; separate files for driverless testing)
datasets.notes: Testing permits only: deployment-permit operations do not file disengagement reports, so commercial robotaxi service is largely absent. Free-text cause descriptions are good material for Claude to categorise.

fetch.instructions: Open the page and download the most recent year's Disengagement and Mileage CSVs.

datasets.name: CPUC autonomous vehicle program quarterly reports
datasets.format: Zip of spreadsheets per quarter and carrier; some cells redacted
datasets.notes: Passenger-service operations: trips, miles, wait times, wheelchair-accessible rides, complaints and incidents depending on the reporting period. This is where you get denominators (miles, trips).

fetch.instructions: Open the page, use 'Download all reports' for the latest deployment-program quarter.

datasets.name: Waymo Safety Impact hub downloads
datasets.format: CSV downloads: rider-only miles and crash data by city, plus human benchmarks
datasets.notes: Company-published. Built on the company's own NHTSA SGO reports plus miles driven by city (San Francisco included). Useful as the denominator and as the claim to check against the raw NHTSA file.

fetch.instructions: Scroll to the download section of the page and save the CSVs.

datasets.name: DataSF: 311 Cases (resident service requests since 2008)
datasets.format: Socrata API; millions of rows, so always query
datasets.notes: The city takes autonomous vehicle incident reports through 311 (sf.gov/report-autonomous-vehicle-incidents). Whether and how those appear in the open dataset needs checking: start with a full-text query and with SELECT DISTINCT on the service fields. The default fetch pulls the 2,000 most recent rows matching 'autonomous'.

datasets.name: DataSF: Traffic Crashes Resulting in Injury
datasets.format: Socrata API / CSV export
datasets.notes: All police-reported injury crashes in the city: the human-driver baseline, by location and time. Companion tables cover parties and victims.

datasets.name: SF Public Works: Autonomous Delivery Device permit program (Public Works Code Sec. 794)
datasets.format: Code text and permit documents (HTML/PDF)
datasets.notes: Rules for sidewalk delivery robots: testing permits only, at most three devices per permittee and nine citywide, 180-day permits. Source text for a rules-as-code or 'is this robot allowed here?' challenge. No incident dataset exists, which is itself a finding.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL and copy Sec. 794 into data/sf-sidewalk-robot-rules/sec794.txt.

datasets.name: EFF Atlas of Surveillance: which US police agencies use which surveillance technology
datasets.format: One CSV, one row per agency-technology pair, with source links
datasets.notes: Filter State == CA and the Bay Area counties. Open-source research, not an official inventory. Device locations are deliberately not included.

datasets.name: San Francisco Surveillance Technology Inventory and policies (Admin Code Chapter 19B)
datasets.format: Web page linking one policy PDF and one impact report PDF per department and technology; biannual inventory report PDFs
datasets.notes: The city's own list: license plate readers, cameras, drones, audio sensors and more, by department, with the approved use policy for each. Biannual reports: https://www.sf.gov/biannual-surveillance-technology-inventory-reports. Pick 5–10 policies and extract retention, sharing and audit rules with Claude.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL, download a handful of policy PDFs into data/sf-surveillance-inventory/.

datasets.name: EFF Data Driven 2: California Dragnet (license plate reader data from 89 agencies)
datasets.format: Spreadsheet
datasets.notes: Scans versus hits per agency: how much plate collection relates to an active investigation. Released 2021, so treat as historical.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL and download the spreadsheet.

datasets.name: NVIDIA Nemotron-PII: synthetic documents with span-level PII/PHI labels
datasets.format: Text with labeled entity spans
datasets.notes: Fully synthetic, so safe to show on screen. Use as the test set for a redaction layer. Announcement: https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/nemotron-pii. Confirm the repo id on the blog page if the fetch fails.

datasets.name: FTC Consumer Sentinel Network data (fraud, identity theft and other reports)
datasets.format: Annual Data Book zip of CSVs (around 100 kB) plus quarterly Tableau dashboards by state and metro area
datasets.notes: Aggregates only, no individual reports. Reports are unverified and self-selected. Find the latest Data Book 'Data Files (Zip archive, CSV files)' link from the page. Metro-area tables include San Francisco-Oakland-Berkeley.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL, go to the Consumer Sentinel Network Data Book page for the latest year, download the CSV zip.

datasets.name: UCI SMS Spam Collection (5,574 labeled SMS messages)
datasets.format: Tab-separated text: label, message
datasets.notes: Old (2012) and mostly UK/Singapore messages, so it under-represents current scams. Good for a fast baseline and for benign 'ham' text.

datasets.name: ealvaradob/phishing-dataset: emails, SMS, URLs and web pages labeled phishing or benign
datasets.format: JSON files per type (texts, urls, webs, combined_reduced), columns text and label
datasets.notes: The dataset ships a loading script that current versions of the `datasets` library refuse to run. Download the JSON files directly from the 'Files' tab instead. The SMS portion separates spam from smishing.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL, 'Files and versions', download texts.json (emails + SMS) or combined_reduced.json.

datasets.name: NVIDIA Aegis 2.0 / Nemotron Content Safety Dataset V2
datasets.format: 33,416 human-LLM interactions (30,007 train / 1,445 validation / 1,964 test) with prompt and response safety labels and violated categories
datasets.notes: Contains explicit harmful text. Use the test split to score a guardrail. May ask you to log in to Hugging Face; set HF_TOKEN if the fetch is refused.

datasets.name: JailbreakBench JBB-Behaviors: 100 harmful and 100 matched benign behaviors in ten categories
datasets.format: CSV: Behavior, Goal, Target, Category, Source
datasets.notes: Small enough to run in full. The benign half is what lets you measure over-refusal. Contains requests, not harmful answers.

datasets.name: lmsys/toxic-chat: real user prompts to a chatbot, labeled for toxicity and jailbreaking
datasets.license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (confirm on the dataset card)
datasets.format: About 10k rows: user_input, model_output, toxicity, jailbreaking
datasets.notes: Real-world distribution: most rows are benign, which makes it good for false-positive rates.

datasets.name: Anthropic discrim-eval: decision prompts varied by age, gender and race
datasets.format: Templated yes/no decision scenarios (loans, housing, hiring and others) with demographic fields
datasets.notes: Run a slice through a model and compare the yes-rate across demographic variants of the same scenario.

datasets.name: Petri and Bloom: open-source automated behavioral auditing and evaluation tools
datasets.format: Python tools. Petri: github.com/safety-research/petri. Bloom: github.com/safety-research/bloom. Combined docs: https://meridianlabs-ai.github.io/petri_bloom/
datasets.notes: Bloom takes a behavior description (for example sycophancy) and generates scenarios, runs them against a target model and scores how often the behavior appears. Petri explores broadly with an auditor agent. Advanced option: setup can eat 20 minutes and runs cost API credits. Keep to 10–20 scenarios.

datasets.name: AI Incident Database (AIID) weekly snapshots
datasets.format: Weekly tar.bz2 (about 120 MB; JSON, CSV and MongoDB dumps) and a small weekly Excel export (about 3 MB)
datasets.notes: Press-reported incidents of AI causing or nearly causing harm, each with linked reports. Take the Excel export for speed. Not a census: coverage follows media attention.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL and download the latest AIID_Excel_Export-YYYYMMDD.xlsx (small) or backup-*.tar.bz2 (full).

datasets.name: MIT AI Risk Repository and AI Incident Tracker
datasets.license: See site (CC BY 4.0 stated for the repository)
datasets.format: Spreadsheet of AI risks coded by a causal taxonomy and a domain taxonomy (7 domains, 23 subdomains); dashboards classifying AIID incidents
datasets.notes: Use the taxonomy as the label set when classifying incidents or the room's concerns. Incident tracker: https://airisk.mit.edu/ai-incident-tracker

fetch.instructions: Open the URL, use the 'copy the Google Sheet / download' link for the repository.

datasets.name: Anthropic Interviewer: 1,250 interview transcripts on how professionals use and feel about AI
datasets.license: Data CC BY, code MIT (per dataset card)
datasets.format: CSV, about 11 MB. Splits: workforce (1,000), creatives (125), scientists (125). Columns: transcript_id, text
datasets.notes: Participants consented to public release. Long transcripts (5k–27k characters): sample 50–100 and have Claude extract trust and safety concerns.

datasets.name: Anthropic values-in-the-wild: taxonomy and frequencies of values Claude expressed in real conversations
datasets.format: CSV: about 3k values with frequencies and a hierarchical taxonomy
datasets.notes: Aggregates only, no conversations. Useful as a vocabulary for 'what should an AI system value in situation X'. Paper: arXiv 2504.15236.

datasets.name: DataSF: Police Department Incident Reports, 2018 to present
datasets.format: Socrata API / CSV export; updated daily
datasets.notes: Reports filed by officers or self-reported online. One incident can have several rows (multiple incident codes): read the dataset explainer before counting (https://sfdigitalservices.gitbook.io/dataset-explainers/sfpd-incident-report-2018-to-present). Aggregate by neighborhood and month; do not plot individual incidents.

datasets.name: Among Us: a sandbox for measuring and detecting agentic deception
datasets.license: See repository (research use; the game IP belongs to Innersloth)
datasets.format: Python sandbox plus logs of 400 complete LLM-agent games and 2,054 game summaries
datasets.notes: LLM agents play a text version of the social-deduction game: impostors deceive, crewmates detect. Use the published logs to build and score a detector without running any games. Paper: arXiv 2504.04072.

datasets.name: Anthropic agentic-misalignment framework
datasets.format: Python framework: fictional corporate scenarios, prompt generation, experiment runner, classifiers
datasets.notes: Scenarios in which a model with a goal and access to email faces replacement or a goal conflict. Useful as a source of 'agent turns against its principal' transcripts for a monitor to read. Runs cost API credits; keep samples small. Paper: arXiv 2510.05179.

datasets.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
datasets.format: One JSON and one CSV file, one row per CVE: vendor, product, dateAdded, dueDate, ransomware flag. Mirror: github.com/cisagov/kev-data
datasets.notes: The authoritative US list of vulnerabilities exploited in the wild. Join with CVE publication dates to measure disclosure-to-exploitation time. Defensive analysis only.

datasets.name: MIT AI Agent Index (2025 edition)
datasets.format: Structured documentation of 30 deployed AI agents: origins, design, capabilities, ecosystem, safety features
datasets.notes: Documents what agent developers disclose and what they do not. Source for a 'safety label' or disclosure-gap scorer. Paper: arXiv 2602.17753.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL and download or copy the per-agent data.

datasets.name: C2PA / Content Credentials open-source tools
datasets.format: Command-line tool (c2patool) and SDKs for reading and writing provenance manifests in images and video
datasets.notes: Tooling, not a dataset: collect your own test images. Most images online carry no credentials, and absence proves nothing.

fetch.instructions: Open the URL; install c2patool from the contentauth organization, or use its Python or JavaScript SDK.
